headline: Approved a $43,184,040 state loan for Bartlett Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility and a City Center Step 3 community investment agreement.
summary: Members approved a consent agenda that included grant applications, contracts, and a $43,184,040 loan for the Bartlett Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility. They also approved a Community Investment Agreement for the City Center Step 3 application. Residents spoke during a budget listening session about the Library, Red Rocks Park, and affordability.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda as presented, including a $43,184,040 State Revolving Fund loan for the Bartlett Bay Wastewater Treatment Facility, 4-0.
Approved the Community Investment Agreement for the City Center Step 3 application and authorized its execution, 4-0.
Agreed on a 9:30-10:30 timeframe for Conversation with a Counselor.

plain_text:
PAGE 1 
DRAFT MINUTES 
 CITY COUNCIL 
       5 OCTOBER 2026 
 
The South Burlington City Council held a regular meeting on Monday, 5 October  
2026, at 6:30 p.m., in the Auditorium, 180 Market Street, and by Zoom. 
 
MEMBERS PRESENT: T. Barritt, Chair; E. Fitzgerald, L. Smith, Dr. B. Zigmund 
 
ALSO PRESENT: J. Baker, City Manager; N. Storellicastro, Deputy City Manager; I. 
Blanchard, Community Development Director; P. Conner, Director of Planning & 
Zoning; B. McCreary, Deputy Director of Public Works for Water Resources; E. 
Towle, Acting Director of Public Works; B. Drapa, Librarian; T. Conley, B. Sirvis, A. 
Pugh, B. Wivey, M. Mittag, A. Allen, K Nanstoll, S. Diggle. T. Lenski, S. Jule, B & C 
Zuccareno, R. Doyle, P. Faylee, A. Rye, S. Babbitt 
 
1. Pledge of Allegiance: 
 
The Pledge of Allegiance was recited. 
 
2. Instructions on exiting building in case of emergency and review of 
technology options: 
 
Ms. Baker provided instructions on emergency exit from the building and 
reviewed technology options. 
  
3. Additions, deletions or changes in the order of Agenda items: 
 
Mr. Storellicastro asked to add an item (6G) to the Consent Agenda to allow him 
to participate in the VERB meeting as he sits on that Board.  Members agreed. 
 
4. Comments and questions from the public not related to the agenda:
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 2 
Ms. Conley, representing neighbors of Brewer Parkway, said following a city 
project on their street, there are now issues that didn’t exist before.  These include 
a huge sinking hole and a significant decrease in water pressure for homes at the 
top of the street.  The latter is so serious that some people cannot flush toilets or 
do laundry.  They asked to be on the 19 October agenda.  Members agreed. 
 
5. Councilors Announcements and Reports on Committee Assignments                                                        
and City Manager’s Report: 
 
Council members reported on recent meetings and events they had attended. 
 
Ms. Baker: Thanked the 500 runners who participated in the event at the Airport 
last week and thanked Adam, Travis, Kate and Brett for a very busy and successful 
week of activities by the Recreation Department. 
 
        The first salt delivery arrived today. 
 
        Regarding the CVOEO proposal, the City is still interested in continuing 
the discussion.  Ms. Baker reached out to a number of groups and has had follow-
up discussions.  These will continue. 
 
       The City Clerk’s office is receiving a number of election calls.  All 
registered voters should be receiving ballots in the mail.  Anyone who does not 
receive a ballot by 13 October, should contact the Clerk’s office. Completed ballots 
can be brought into the Clerk’s office or placed in the designated receptacles in 
the City.  Anyone choosing to mail in a completed ballot should do so by 20 
October to ensure that it is received by Election Day. 
 
6. Consent Agenda: 
a. Consider and Sign Disbursements 
b. Authorize the Deputy Director of Water Resources to apply for 
the MS4 3-acre Adoption Grant from the State of Vermont 
Agency of Natural Resources – Department of Environmental 
Conservation on behalf of the City of South Burlington 
Stormwater Utility 
c. Approve Resolution 2026-14 committing to match grant funds 
and submittal of a letter of support for the Northern Border 
Regional Commission Catalyst Program Grant funding to support 
Phase II of the Walk-Bike Bridge
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 3 
d. Approve the construction and inspection contracts for the 
Kennedy Drive Pond 7 Stormwater Project.  This includes (1) 
approve the award of construction contract for the planned 
Kennedy Drive Pond 7 stormwater project and authorize the 
Deputy Director of Water Resources to execute and manage the 
contract. And (2) the Deputy Director of Water Resources to 
execute and manage the construction services contract for the 
same project. 
e. Authorize staff to apply for the Climate Catalyst Innovation Fund 
2026 Grant 
f. Accept the terms of the proposed loan agreement and authorize 
the City Council Chair and Finance Director to sign the agreement 
with the Vermont Bond Bank for a State Revolving Fund loan of 
$43,184,040 for the purpose of construction on the Bartlett Bay 
Wastewater Treatment Facility 
  
Mr. McCreary explained items “b” and “d” regarding upgrading of streams and 
the City’s adopting permits from residential communities when they have met 
State standards.  The City helps design and construct projects. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald then moved to approve the Consent Agenda as presented.  Mr. 
Smith seconded.  The motion passed 4-0. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald noted the doubling of diesel fuel expenses in recent months and 
credited staff, especially Ms. Blanchard, for the submittal of grant applications. 
 
7. Hold a the FY28 Budget Community Listening Session: 
 
Ms. Baker noted the budget survey and budget schedule on the City’s Website. 
 
Mr. Barritt then asked for public comment which was received as follows: 
 
Ms. Wivey: At a recent party she attended, many people were talking about their 
love of the Library for many different reasons.  She hoped this would continue so 
the Library stays strong. 
 
The Executive Director of the City Center Collaborative asked to continue the 
$75,000 funding for continued support of the Collaborative.  They are currently 
implementing their 5-year plan and will be happy to come back and provide 
details.
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 4 
 
Ms. Pugh: Asked to add more than $25,000 for Red Rocks Park.  She noted it is 
the only public access to the Lake.  She added praise for the Library and for the 
addition of restaurants on Market Street. 
 
Ms. Sirvis: Asked the Council to keep affordability in mind and expressed 
concern that the word “affordable” has been taken out of the name of the 
Housing Committee. 
 
Ms. Allen: Also asked to keep affordability a concern.  She asked to lean into the 
economic development plan so the City doesn’t have to rely so much on property 
taxes. 
 
Following public comment, Ms. Baker stressed that the number the Council heard 
at its last meeting were not a recommendation, just a data point. 
 
8. Receive and Approve the Community Investment Agreement for the 
City Center Step 3 application (formerly the Downtown Designation) 
and execute the agreement: 
 
Ms. Blanchard explained that the Agreement is a requirement of the application.  
It is an opportunity to bring the community and others on board.  The Agreement 
was worked on with the City Center Collaborative and most of the responsibilities 
of the Agreement will fall to the City and to the Collaborative.  Other entities can 
be “Champions.”  This is preliminary to submitting the application.  Staff will 
reach out for additional signatures. 
 
Mr. Conner outlined the benefits the City will receive if the application is 
approved, including: 
 
a. State funding 
b. Higher position on competitive lists for grants 
c. Tax benefits to property owners 
d. Greater ability to assign special districts 
e. Additional ability for traffic calming and signage 
f. Streamlined reviews for trees in the State right-of-way 
g. Act 250 Tier 1A qualification 
 
Mr. Conner noted that most major downtowns have this designation.  The 
window to do this just opened this summer.  Ms. Baker added that the State has
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 5 
created the opportunity for this kind of vibrancy.  Mr. Conner said staff will be 
back to submit the full application. 
 
Ms. Fitzgerald moved to approve the Community Investment Agreement for the 
City Center Step 3 Application as presented and execute the Agreement.  Dr. 
Zigmund seconded.  The motion passed 4-0. 
 
9. Receive the FY27 Policy Priorities and Strategies Report #1: 
 
Ms. Baker presented two updates: 
 
a. Staff uses the report internally as part of administrative meetings 
b. Conversations the City Council wanted to engage in have been 
calendared 
 
Upcoming discussions will focus on a growth management plan and thermal 
heating. 
 
Mr. Barritt asked if any projects endured more pain than others.  Ms. Baker replied 
that none come to mind other than the bid environment.   
 
Ms. Fitzgerald asked when the new water tower will be in service.  Ms. Towle said 
construction is complete, and they are now working with CWD regarding the 
turnover of ownership.  Her guess was that it would be in service in the spring. 
 
10. Discuss the next steps for Conversation with a Counselor: 
 
Suggestions included: “office hours,” possibly a “remote” option, possible middle 
of the week hours, joining with an HOA group, a possible “invite a counselor” and 
keeping the same availability and then trying something new. 
 
Mr. Mittag suggested a room in the Library which might attract more of the public.  
Ms. Sirvis said this could allow for a Zoom option as well.  Ms. Drapa said that 
would be best if it started after 9 a.m.   
 
Ms. Baker will have staff put together a sign-up and put together an ‘invite a 
counselor’ language. 
 
Members agreed on a 9:30-10:30 timeframe.
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 6 
11. Review the Significant Agenda Items for the Council’s 15 October 
2026 Special Joint Meeting with the Planning Commission: 
 
a. Receive and Discuss the draft Parks & Open Space Master Plan 
 
12. Review the Significant Agenda Items for the Council’s 19 October 
2026 City Council Meeting: 
 
a. Receive an update on the Building & Thermal Implementation 
Plan and consider what actions to take in parallel 
b. Approve the Downtown Application Submittal 
c. Discuss the Old Farm Road development agreement and potential 
CHIP application 
d. Legislative Advocacy Agenda: Receive recommendation areas for 
legislative advocacy and discuss Council priorities 
 
13. Consider entering into Executive Session pursuant to 1 V.S.A. 
Section 313(a)(1)(F) and (2) for the purpose of receiving confidential 
attorney-client communication and discussing the negotiation of real 
estate lease or purchase options, specifically 1720 Spear Street: 
 
Mr. Smith moved that the Council make a specific finding that premature general 
public knowledge of the Council’s receipt of attorney-client communications and 
discussion on the negotiating or securing of real estate purchase or lease options 
clearly place this public body at a substantial disadvantage.  Ms. Fitzgerald 
seconded.  The motion passed 4-0. 
 
Mr. Smith then moved that the City Council enter into Executive Session under 1 
U.S.A. Section 313(a)(1)(F) and (a)(2) for the purpose of receiving confidential 
attorney-client communications and discussing the negotiating for the securing of 
real estate purchase or lease options, inviting into the session Ms. Baker, Mr. 
Storellicastro, Mr. Conner, Ms. Towle, and Mr. McNeil.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  
The motion passed 4-0. 
 
The Council entered executive session at 8:11 p.m. 
 
Mr. Smith moved to exit executive session.  Dr. Zigmund seconded.  The motion 
passed 4-0.  The Council exited executive session at 9:01 p.m.
CITY COUNCIL 5 OCTOBER 2026 PAGE 7 
As there was no further business to come before the Council Mr. Smith moved to                   
adjourn.  Ms. Fitzgerald seconded.  Motion passed unanimously.  The meeting 
was adjourned at 9:02 p.m.
